EXP-01 NFP volatility.verdict: SUPPORTED: NFP days show systematically wider daily ranges (+14 pips median, p=0.0049 vs all days, p=0.0041 vs non-NFP Fridays). Daily data confirms the necessary condition for the 100-pip intraday claim; the 30-second/100-pip spike itself is an intraday microstructure event documented in broker studies cited in README.

EXP-02 Pip/leverage liquidation.verdict: SUPPORTED: 0.5 lots = $5.0/pip; -100 pips = $-500 on a $200 account (2.5x the account). Only 40 adverse pips wipes it — NFP routinely exceeds that intraday. The story's liquidation is arithmetically inevitable, not a broken rule.

EXP-03 Expectancy Monte Carlo.verdict: SUPPORTED: E = 0.400R/trade (>0); breakeven is 40.0%, edge is +16pp. At 1% risk, 500-trade ruin(50%) ≈ 0.0%, wipeout ≈ 0.00%; gambler sizing ruin ≈ 97%. $500→$1,800 (≈3.6x over ~77 trades) is within the technician distribution's upper-but-plausible tail, not a fantasy — compounding at +0.4%/trade compounds.

EXP-04 Friction audit.verdict: SUPPORTED: 1.625 pips/trade × 1200 + gaps = 1995 pips/lot/yr. At 20x leverage ≈ 399%/yr, at 10x ≈ 200%/yr — the MPRA 200-400% band replicates exactly. At institutional 1x leverage the same friction is ≈20%/yr. Leverage, not strategy, is the dominant P&L term for hyperactive retail.

EXP-05 Loss-rate benchmark.verdict: SUPPORTED WITH NUANCE: modern 12-month rolling disclosures average ≈71.0% (TIC 69.9, BrokerRank 71.0, KNF 72.2); the story's '74-89%' matches ESMA's original band and the long-horizon AMF 89% (4-yr tracking) — i.e. the longer you stay, the closer to 89%. Signal-group survivorship (1/50 screenshots) is the expected artefact of a ~70-90% loss base rate.

EXP-06 Sharpe/drawdown.verdict: SUPPORTED: 100→92 is 8.0% DD (story says 8% ✓); $12k×7% = $840 ✓. Story 8-month sample Sharpe ≈ 2.87 — very-good, near the suspicious boundary: honest caveat is n=8 is far too short to quote a Sharpe. Noise Sharpe ≈ 0.29, persistent-edge Sharpe ≈ 1.32: ladder holds. 15% kill-switch breach ≈ 1.3% over 500 trades at 1% risk — a real constraint, not decoration.

EXP-07 B-book aggregate.verdict: SUPPORTED: even at near-fair 48%/0.9R, friction ($3.1/trade) drags mean client to $-1191 over 100 trades; only 9.5% profitable — inside the 11-31% profitable band implied by 69-89% loss disclosures. Dealer nets ≈ $118.3M per 10M trades before overhead: the aggregate edge is structural, not conspiratorial. BIS $9.6T/day makes $3T among top-5 LPs arithmetically ordinary (31%).

EXP-08 Slippage/latency.verdict: SUPPORTED: daily σ ≈ 0.0046 → retail 200ms latency costs ≈ 0.031 pips/trade vs colo ≈ 0.00069 pips — a ~45x gap. Assumed 0.35-pip slippage is 1.7% of the 20-pip gross edge: material but not edge-destroying for a 1.5R swing system; fatal for sub-5-pip scalps. Colocation 'speed of light' claim is directionally correct physics.
